title: Delegation of Authority and Procedural Empowerment
summary: The concept of the 'authorized officer' evolves from a traditional hierarchical delegation (where a Commissioner delegates specific tasks like port clearance or document certification) to a modern digital-integrated framework. Recent instruments incorporate electronic system interactions and AEO-specific compliance reporting, shifting the officer's role from manual oversight to system-based verification and accountability.

evolution.scope: Expanded from administrative/clearance tasks to include financial cost recovery and AEO compliance monitoring.
evolution.procedure: Transitioned from purely manual/physical oversight to digital/system-based authorization and electronic filing.

timeline.change: Expands the scope of authorized officers to include financial oversight of MOT and incidental expenses.
Formalizes the role of the authorized officer in receiving and processing AEO-specific error reporting.

Port Clearance: The master of a vessel is required to submit an application for port clearance at least twenty-four hours prior to the vessel's intended departure.
The Commissioner of Customs or an authorized officer may allow the submission of the application within a shorter timeframe for recorded special reasons.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs has the authority to grant permission for a reduced application submission timeline for port clearance.
The Commissioner of Customs issues general instructions regarding the submission of export bills and other documents necessary for port clearance.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: Registered vessel masters are permitted to submit port clearance applications and required export documents electronically through the customs computerized system, with such electronic submissions being deemed duly signed.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is responsible for prescribing the format of the export manifest required to be submitted by the vessel master.
Export Manifest: Vessel masters must submit two copies of a signed export manifest containing a detailed description of all goods to be exported.
The export manifest must separately list any imported goods or stores that remain on board and have not been landed, transshipped, or otherwise accounted for.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer receives the export manifest, bills of export, and other required documents from the master and is authorized to interrogate the master regarding the vessel's destination and departure.
Import Manifest: The provisions governing the amendment of the import manifest under Section 45 are applicable to the export manifest submitted under Section 54, with necessary modifications.

member_objects.resolved_text:
3[215A. Supply of information and copy of decisions.- (1) Upon an application of a person directly interested in a decision taken by a customs officer under this Act, the Commissioner of Customs or an officer authorised by him shall, subject to payment by the applicant of a fee specified by the Board, deliver within 15 (fifteen) days of the application, a true copy of that decision with a certificate that it is a true copy :

Provided that a copy or other copy or reproduction of the certified copy shall not be admissible as evidence or otherwise accepted in any court of law.

(2) Upon an application of a person directly interested in a decision taken or omitted to have been taken by a customs officer, the Commissioner of Customs shall inform that person in writing within a period of 60 days of the application the reasons for such decision or omission.]

Customs Decision: A person directly interested in a decision taken by a customs officer has the right to obtain a certified true copy of that decision upon application and payment of the prescribed fee.

A person directly interested in a decision or omission by a customs officer has the right to receive a written explanation of the reasons for such action or inaction from the Commissioner of Customs within a specified period.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs or an authorized officer is responsible for providing a certified true copy of a customs decision to an interested applicant within a defined timeframe upon payment of the specified fee.
The Commissioner of Customs is mandated to provide a written explanation for a decision or omission to an interested applicant within the stipulated time limit.
Documentary Evidence: Any copy or reproduction of a certified true copy of a customs decision is explicitly declared inadmissible as evidence in any court of law.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to specify the fee payable by an applicant for obtaining a certified true copy of a customs decision.

Port Clearance: The master of a vessel is required to submit an application for port clearance at least twenty-four hours before the vessel's intended departure. The Commissioner of Customs or an authorized officer may permit a shorter application period under special recorded circumstances.
Master: The master is responsible for applying for port clearance, delivering necessary documentation such as the export manifest and bills of export, and answering inquiries regarding the vessel's departure and destination. When acting as a registered user, the master may fulfill these requirements by transmitting documents to the customs computer system.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs has the authority to approve a reduced timeframe for port clearance applications and provides general instructions for the documentation required during the clearance process.
Export Manifest: The master must deliver an export manifest in duplicate, which specifies all goods to be exported and details items carried over from the import manifest that remain on board. The document must follow the prescribed form and be signed by the master, or transmitted electronically if the master is a registered user.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer receives the export manifest, bills of export, and other required documents, and has the authority to examine the master regarding the vessel's departure and destination.
Registered User: A master who is a registered user may submit applications, export manifests, and other required documents via the customs computer system, with such transmissions legally deemed as signed by the master.
Customs Computerised Entry Processing Sy: The customs computer system serves as the digital platform for registered users to transmit export manifests and other clearance documents, substituting for physical document submission.

Export Manifest: items carried over from the import manifest

Cargo Declaration: This form serves as the official application for amending a cargo declaration or submitting a supplementary cargo declaration.
Applicants must provide detailed information about the transport, importer, exporter, and the specific nature of the goods being amended.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs or an authorized officer is the designated authority to receive and review applications for cargo declaration amendments.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is the governing body responsible for issuing the official administrative orders and forms for customs procedures.
Customs Clearance: The application requires the user to disclose whether the goods have been examined, removed from the port of arrival, or if a bill of entry has already been filed, as these factors influence the amendment process.
